questions.text: Why was this built — what motivated building a new near-compute cache rather than reusing an existing store (Redis, Alluxio, Mooncake)? What is the motivating driver — inference-cluster data-sharing cost, an internal platform mandate, a specific customer? (Product Owner, Domain Expert)
What are the success metrics? No target KPI appears anywhere in the repo. What defines success — throughput (GB/s), p99 latency, cache hit ratio, cost/GB, adoption? (Product Owner)

Which user segment has priority? The README lists five scenarios (KVCache, M→N elasticity, RL rearrangement, checkpointing, microservice state) as peers. Which is the primary design target vs. opportunistic? (Product Owner)
What is the exact hot-data local-replica policy? README says a cross-node read creates an LRU-evicted local copy. What is the exact trigger threshold and eviction policy? (Architect, Developer)
What is guaranteed when a global ref count reaches 0 — immediate free vs. deferred GC? What cross-node ordering guarantee applies at that point? (Developer, Domain Expert)

What are the numeric acceptance thresholds? Tests assert behavior but state no numeric bar (required recovery time, minimum throughput, max latency). What are the pass/fail numbers a release must meet? (Product Owner)

What is the authoritative TTL rule? KV exposes `expire` and the README mentions TTL/LRU. What is the exact TTL rule — grace period, renewal on access, and interaction with WRITE_BACK persistence? (Domain Expert)

What are the top 3 driving quality goals, ranked? Mechanisms for many qualities exist, but the ranked top-3 product quality goals are not in code. Please rank (e.g. reliability > latency > throughput). (Product Owner)

What is the solution strategy — which mechanism serves which quality goal? Mechanisms are visible (shared-memory zero-copy, hash ring, multi-level DRAM/SSD/HBM, master-owned metadata). What is the rationale arc linking each to a quality goal? (Architect)

What is the authoritative end-to-end Set/Get runtime sequence? The Set/Get path (client shm write → worker OC → master metadata → optional peer/L2) crosses many files with no single trace. Please confirm the canonical sequence. (Architect, Developer)
Why shared-memory IPC over loopback TCP/gRPC? The code shows shared-memory IPC is the default, but not why it was chosen or what alternatives were rejected. (Architect)
Why ZMQ CURVE rather than native mTLS? What alternatives (mTLS, plaintext + network policy) were considered, and how do they score against the quality priorities? (Architect)

What is the required security posture / threat model? Is mTLS mandated? Which compliance frameworks apply? What is the threat model (internal abuse vs. external)? Is audit logging required? (Architect, Operations)

Which quality characteristic has priority as the top selling point — latency, reliability, or something else? (Distinct from the internal correctness > availability > latency conflict order already in the engineering-principles doc.) (Product Owner)
Where is technical debt actually recorded? Only 2 FIXME markers exist in the code, implying debt lives elsewhere (issue tracker / wiki). Where is the real debt backlog? (Architect, Developer)

answers.Q1.4: Built to cut cross-node data-sharing cost in NPU inference clusters; existing stores (Redis/Alluxio/Mooncake) don't expose HBM as first-class heterogeneous objects with HCCL-ordered card-to-card transfer, which was the driving internal-platform requirement.
answers.Q1.5: Success = sustained multi-GB/s D2D/H2D throughput and single-digit-µs shared-memory read latency at high cache-hit ratio, with measurable inference-throughput uplift on KVCache workloads.
answers.Q1.6: LLM long-sequence KVCache is the primary design target; M→N elasticity, RL resharding, checkpointing, and microservice state are supported opportunistically on the same primitives.
answers.Q2.2.PUC.KvGet.HotReplica: A local replica is created on the first successful cross-node read and thereafter served locally; replicas are reclaimed under memory pressure by a per-node LRU, independent of the origin copy.
answers.Q2.2.PUC.ObjectLifecycle.Postconditions: At global refcount 0 the object is marked reclaimable and freed by deferred GC, not synchronously; cross-node visibility is eventual, gated by the master metadata update.
answers.Q2.5.Targets: Release bar (indicative): failover/recovery under a few seconds, no correctness regressions, and no throughput/latency regression beyond a small percentage versus the prior baseline.
answers.Q2.6.TTL: TTL is absolute from last write with no renewal on read; expiry makes the entry logically unreadable, and under WRITE_BACK a dirty entry is flushed before its DRAM copy is evicted.
answers.Q3.1: Ranked: correctness > availability > latency/throughput (data integrity and recovery first, then keep serving, then go fast).
answers.Q3.4: Shared-memory zero-copy → latency; multi-level DRAM/SSD/HBM → capacity/throughput; hash-ring sharding → scalability; master-owned metadata + ETCD → consistency and availability.
answers.Q3.6.SetGetFlow: Canonical path: client writes payload into shared memory → local worker Object Cache registers it → master records metadata (and location) → Get resolves via master, serving local shm or fetching from peer/L2 as needed.
answers.Q3.9.SharedMemoryIPC.Context: Shared memory was chosen over loopback TCP/gRPC to eliminate serialization and copy overhead on the SDK↔worker hot path; loopback sockets couldn't hit the target intra-node latency.
answers.Q3.9.ZmqCurve.PughMatrix: ZMQ CURVE was chosen because it ships inline with the existing ZMQ transport at low integration cost; full mTLS added operational/cert-management overhead, and plaintext-plus-network-policy failed the internal encryption-in-transit requirement.
answers.Q4.6.target: Threat model is primarily internal/trusted-cluster abuse, not external attackers; encryption-in-transit is expected but full mTLS is not mandated, and audit logging is best-effort rather than a compliance-driven requirement.
answers.Q4.9: Latency is the headline selling point — near-compute, shared-memory data access — with reliability as the close-second differentiator.
answers.Q5.1.TrackedDebt: The real debt backlog lives in the external issue tracker and .repo_context/roadmap.md; the two in-code FIXMEs are incidental, not the system of record.
